props.title: 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days
props.initialSlug: Time runs out. Freedom has a price.

sections.content: 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days stands as a masterwork of Romanian New Wave cinema, delivering an unflinching look at life under Ceaușescu's communist regime. Director Cristian Mungiu crafts a devastating portrait of two college students seeking an illegal abortion, using long takes and stark naturalism that influenced films like Beyond the Hills (2012) and Child's Pose (2013). The film's claustrophobic atmosphere and real-time sequences create unbearable tension, similar to the sustained dread in The Death of Mr. Lazarescu (2005), another Romanian New Wave landmark.

sections.content: Mungiu's technique of using minimal camera movement and extended scenes revolutionized contemporary European cinema. His influence can be seen in works like Two Days, One Night (2014) and Son of Saul (2015), which similarly employ intimate handheld camerawork to create immediate, visceral experiences. The film's exploration of female friendship under systemic oppression connects thematically to works like Never Rarely Sometimes Always (2020) and Happening (2021). SUBHEAD: Impact on Social Realist Cinema

The film's success helped establish a new standard for social realist drama, inspiring works like Mustang (2015) and Silent Night (2021) that examine women's rights and bodily autonomy through an unflinching lens. Mungiu's decision to set the story in 1987 Romania creates powerful parallels with contemporary abortion debates, similar to how Vera Drake (2004) used 1950s Britain to comment on modern reproductive rights issues.
